body:
Founder-supplied "SSH Transport & Identity" implementation spec + Amendment 1 (guest tier &
channel gating). Two real problems: plaintext telnet session hijack reaching a bank/AH/bazaar,
and nameless identity (any account with value is takeable by anyone who reads/guesses the name).
Stage 1 (telnet economy+chat gate) named explicitly as "the actual security fix... ship it
first."

Real, checked finding before implementing anything: Amendment 1 assumed telnet characters were
already ephemeral. Checked directly -- they're real, IDUNA-persisted, named characters
(mudCharCache). Raised to the founder rather than silently stripping real persistence or
ignoring the spec. Founder's real, live-tested resolution: reconnect-by-name doesn't reliably
resume a character as actually played -- treated as this tier's real, intended, permanent model
going forward.

Shipped: player.isGuest (true for telnet, false for headless/Town-GUI which already has real
WOTAN identity). guestGate blocks bank/bazaar/ah + say/tell/yell/guild/party-chat at the real
server-layer dispatch point, with an explain-the-upgrade message (not a bare denial) + structured
log line per attempt. Connect banner states guest scope before the name prompt. Permitted:
movement/combat/jobs/subjobs/party+linkshell membership/quests/exploration/dungeons/NMs.

11 new tests. Live-verified via a real, unmocked Python socket script against a throwaway
isolated instance -- the real, live production :2323 server was never touched or restarted.
GOWORK=off go build/vet/test ./... clean.

Full spec + phased NORTHSTAR checked in: docs2/SSH_TRANSPORT_IDENTITY_{SPEC,AMENDMENT_1,
NORTHSTAR}.md. Stages 2-8 (GUI TLS, process isolation, SSH listener, identity binding, port 22,
device-flow hardening, telnet deprecation) scoped, not started.

GoblinFoxDragon commit d5b2ef6.
